### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, A22 was executed exactly once in every case (participation 100%, mean 1.0 occurrence per trace); in the later window it appears in only about half of the cases (about 102 in 200, mean 0.51), still at most once per case. [OCC001]
- A27, A28 and A33 were not observed at all in the earlier window (0 of 200 traces); in the later window each appears in about 49 in 100 cases, once per case, at a median event position near the middle of the trace (about 0.48–0.50 of trace length). [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, POS001, POS002, POS003]
- In the later window, A22 and each of A27, A28, A33 never occur in the same case (co-occurrence 0): A22 runs alone in about 51 in 100 cases and the three new activities run together in the other about 49 in 100, so they behave as mutually exclusive alternatives. [REL006, REL007, REL008, REL012, REL013, REL014]
- The surrounding order is stable: A21 precedes A22 in every case where A22 runs and precedes each of A27/A28/A33 in every case where they run; both A22 and the new activities precede A23. In the earlier window this amounted to A21 → A22 → A23 in all cases. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL009, REL010, REL011]
- The three new activities show no fixed order among themselves: for example, A27 precedes A28 in about 23 in 100 cases while A28 precedes A27 in about 27 in 100, with similar mixed proportions for the other pairs. [REL012, REL013, REL014]
- The distance from A21 to A23 was always 2 event positions in the earlier window; in the later window it is 2 positions in about 51 in 100 cases and 4 positions in about 49 in 100, consistent with one intermediate activity being replaced by three. [LAG001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a structural change in the segment between A21 and A23. In the earlier window every case ran A21 → A22 → A23; in the later window about half the cases still do, while in the other half A22 is replaced by a block of three activities — A27, A28 and A33 — executed between A21 and A23 in no fixed internal order, with A22 and this block never occurring in the same case. The hypothesis rests on direct and mutually consistent evidence: the participation flip (A22 from 100% to about 51%; A27/A28/A33 from 0% to about 49%), the zero co-occurrence between A22 and the new block, the unchanged ordering of A21 before and A23 after the segment, and the A21–A23 distance changing from always 2 to 2 or 4 event positions. The volume of qualifying evidence (22 items against roughly 0.26 expected in an unchanged process) is far beyond what random re-splits of a stable process produce. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, REL001, REL005, REL006, REL009, REL012, LAG001, POS001]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out: zero participation in the earlier window only shows that A27, A28 and A33 were not observed in those 200 traces, so a pre-existing alternative path used in fewer than roughly 1–2 in 100 cases could have gone unsampled; the evidence therefore cannot distinguish a newly inserted block from a strong shift toward a previously very rare alternative. [OCC002, OCC003, OCC004]
